summary: Vegetarian paella with baby artichokes and green beans: saffron-infused broth, a grated onion and tomato sofrito and paella rice simmered without stirring in a 14-inch pan, then crisped about 2 minutes at the end to form the socarrat crust.
glance: 1.5 cups paella rice (not Uncle Ben's or basmati) with 3.5 cups clear vegetable broth
about 8 minutes simmering, 10 minutes lower, 3 covered, then a couple minutes to crisp the crust
14-inch paella pan, or a non-cast-iron skillet
faq: What makes a paella a paella?
The real main event is beautifully cooked, tomato and saffron infused short-grain rice with a caramelized crust on the bottom, called socarrat, not the seafood.
What rice should I use for paella?
Proper paella rice, such as the Matiz brand the author uses. Don't use Uncle Ben's or basmati.
How do I get the socarrat crust?

Don't stir at any point. After the rice is cooked, cover the pan and cook 3 more minutes, then with the foil on raise the heat to medium-high and cook a couple more minutes until you hear a bit of crackling. You want a serious crust but not a burned one. Rest covered about 5 minutes.
What saffron should I buy?

Saffron is the world's most expensive spice by weight, so it's often adulterated. Buy the whole stigma, not powder, from a brand you trust. You only need a pinch, toasted a minute in a foil packet and crushed into the broth.
What kind of vegetable stock?
A clear, mild broth not dominated by any one vegetable. Many are thick and soupy or full of MSG, so be choosy; the author likes Seitenbacher.
What pan do I need?
A 14-inch paella pan works, but you can also do it successfully in a non-cast-iron skillet, or buy an inexpensive dedicated paella pan.

summary: Sicilian spaghetti with pan-roasted cauliflower, from the Herbivoracious cookbook: cauliflower boiled 5 minutes then browned in a hot skillet with garlic, fennel and chile, tossed with orange, capers, raisins, pine nuts and spaghetti; 30 minutes.
glance: boil 5 minutes, then pan-roast in high heat until deeply browned
orange zest, raisins, capers, pine nuts, chile flakes and fennel
Vegetarian; vegan if you omit the Parmesan
faq: What are the classic Sicilian flavors in this pasta?
Orange zest, raisins, capers, pine nuts, chile flakes and fennel. Each bite is a little surprise that might be sweet, spicy, salty, toasty, herbaceous or all of the above.
How do I get the cauliflower caramelized?

Keep the heat high and don't toss too often, so the surfaces on the bottom of the pan brown. A cast-iron skillet is preferred. The cauliflower is first boiled 5 minutes and drained, so it cooks through quickly.
Can I make the pasta and cauliflower at the same time?
Yes. With all ingredients ready, boil the pasta while you pan-fry the cauliflower and everything finishes together. Reuse the cauliflower's boiling water for the spaghetti.
What does the orange zest do?
The author particularly loves it in the final garnish, where it becomes fragrant from the heat of the pasta.
How do I make it vegan?
Omit the grated Parmesan.

summary: Vegetarian potstickers (gyoza) with a tempeh filling: pan-fried tempeh crumbled with browned cabbage, green onion, rice wine, soy sauce and cornstarch in 48 wrappers, fried 1-2 minutes, steamed with 1/3 cup of water about 3 minutes, then crisped; makes about 48.
glance: about 48 dumplings (at least 4 per person as an appetizer)
1-2 minutes, add 1/3 cup water and cover about 3 minutes, then cook off the water
1 pound tempeh, cabbage, green onions, rice wine, soy sauce, cornstarch
quick-freeze without touching, then bag; cook without defrosting
faq: What is the best vegetarian potsticker filling?

The author's choice is tempeh, sauteed first to develop flavor, then crumbled and mashed with the other ingredients; it gives just the right bite. Most vegetarian potstickers go wrong by using too many vegetables, which leach water and add a distracting crunch.
Why are they called potstickers?

They're first fried in a lightly oiled pan until they brown and stick a bit, then water is added and the pan covered to steam the tops and release the bottoms, then the lid comes off and the remaining water cooks off.
How do you make potstickers crispy?
Keep cooking after steaming until the water is totally gone, otherwise they won't be crispy. Fry flat-side down in a single layer 1-2 minutes until dark golden brown first.
Can I freeze potstickers?
Yes. Quick freeze them without touching each other, then bag when solid. They can be cooked later without defrosting; allow a little more time.
What are other names for potstickers?
Jiaozi (Chinese, pretty much any dumpling), guotie (Chinese, specifically pan-fried), gyoza (Japanese, any dumpling) and yaki-gyoza (pan-fried).
What dipping sauce goes with them?
A mix of soy sauce, rice vinegar, hot-chili sesame oil and thin rings of green onion, tasted for salt, vinegar and heat balance. The author likes it pretty vinegary.

summary: Artichaut marinieres: baby artichokes steamed in a bath of dry vermouth with butter, shallot, garlic, parsley and thyme, like moules mariniere, then served in a bowl with grilled bread to sop up the artichoke-flavored broth; 30 minutes.
glance: 1 1/2 pounds baby artichokes, kept in lemon water
1 1/2 cups dry vermouth (or a light, unoaked white wine)
grilled artisan bread brushed with olive oil

summary: Saag with collard greens, kale and spinach: greens cooked about 45 minutes with a warm spice mixture until completely soft, then finished with yogurt instead of cream; 15 minutes active, 1 hour total, serves 4 as part of a larger Indian dinner.
glance: 4 as part of a larger Indian dinner
1 bunch kale, 1 bunch collards and a 10-ounce package of frozen spinach
about 45 minutes, covered, until completely tender
yield: 4 as part of a larger Indian dinner
faq: What is saag?

The whole family of dishes made of long-cooked leafy greens, also transliterated sak or sag. In the Punjab and Pakistan, where these dishes apparently originated, it can be made with any dark leafy green.
How is this different from saag paneer?

Saag paneer, spinach cooked with cream and cubes of fresh cheese, is delicious but often so rich it obscures the flavors of the greens and spices. This version uses kale, collards and spinach with yogurt instead of cream.
Why use some spinach?
The author recommends about half spinach for a more delicate flavor and softer texture. Mustard greens would also be delicious.
How do I wash the greens?
Triple-wash them in a bowl, not a colander, in three changes of warm water. Any grit will ruin the dish.
How do I add the yogurt without it breaking?
Turn off the heat, let the greens cool slightly, stir in the yogurt, and reheat gently without bringing it all the way toward a simmer.
How soft should the greens be?
Completely softened, about 45 minutes. This isn't the place for lightly steamed, crunchy vegetables.

summary: Gorditas with roasted mushrooms: thick masa harina rounds toasted 2 minutes per side on a dry skillet, then fried about 45 seconds per side at 360°F, split and filled with oven-roasted button mushrooms in a spiced tomato paste sauce; makes 14.
glance: 14 gorditas, serves 6 as a main course
Prep 1 hr, cook 45 min, total 1 hr 45 min
dry skillet 4 minutes total, then fry at about 360°F, about 45 seconds per side
2 1/2 pounds button mushrooms roasted at 450°F, about 40 minutes
yield: 14 gorditas, serves 6 as a main course
faq: What are gorditas?
Thick, homemade corn tortillas that are shallow fried, then split and topped with whatever you like. They are close cousins of the arepa and the pupusa.
Is making gorditas hard?

A bit of a project, not a weeknight meal: you make and shape the dough, toast the gorditas on a dry skillet, then fry them in a good bit of oil. They make a fun weekend dinner, and kids can help shape the dough.
How do I cook gorditas?

Flatten 64-gram balls into circles about 3 1/2 inches across and 1/3 inch thick. Cook in a dry medium skillet 2 minutes per side until leathery, then fry in oil at about 360°F until golden brown, about 45 seconds a side, flipping carefully with tongs.
How should the dough feel?
Supple and somewhat moist. If not, add a few more tablespoons of water. Let the masa harina and water hydrate 15 minutes before kneading in the oil, salt and baking powder.
Why roast the mushrooms?
Quartered and oven-roasted at 450°F they develop flavor and lose excess water, leaving large toothsome bites, then they're finished with a spiced tomato paste mixture to make a bit of sauce.
What do I serve on gorditas?
Salsa, crumbly Mexican cheese or feta, stewed black beans, pickled cabbage and cilantro.

summary: Fried pita bread with fava beans and zucchini: torn pita fry-toasted in olive oil, then tossed back with sauteed zucchini, olives, cooked fava or garbanzo beans, harissa and cherry tomatoes; a one-pot meal for 1, ready in about 15 minutes.
glance: 1 as a hearty one-pot meal (multiply as needed)
1 slightly stale pita, torn and browned in olive oil
2 teaspoons harissa (less if you aren't into heat)
yield: 1 as a hearty one-pot meal (multiply as needed)
faq: What can I do with stale pita?
Tear it into bite-sized pieces, fry-toast it in olive oil until browned in a fair number of spots, then garnish with whatever is on hand for a late-night snack that might pass for a meal.
Can I change the ingredients?

Yes, the dish is infinitely malleable: use chickpeas instead of fava beans, cauliflower instead of zucchini, or corn tortillas instead of pita for something like chilaquiles. A fried egg on top is a valid option.
Why return the bread at the end?
Add it back only at the end and toss through, because you don't want to make it soggy, so loosen the sauce with just a bit of water.
What harissa should I use?
The author recommends Mustapha's harissa, which is hot but also has a fantastic citrusy complexity.
How do I garnish it?
With plenty of good olive oil, halved cherry tomatoes, parsley, and optionally zucchini blossoms.

summary: Grilled achiote-rubbed butternut squash tacos: butternut slabs rubbed with achiote paste and grilled with charred poblanos, tossed with crema and cilantro, and served on soft corn tortillas with red onion, queso panela and hot sauce; serves 8 as part of a feast.
glance: 8 as part of a feast (32 soft corn tortillas, two per taco)
1 large butternut in 1/2-inch slabs, rubbed with 2 ounces achiote paste
3, charred, then steamed 10 minutes in a covered bowl to loosen the skins
Vegetarian and gluten-free; vegan without the cheese and crema
faq: What is achiote?

The red color comes from annatto seed, the same plant used to color cheddar cheese. It is typically sold in a small brick mixed with spices, vinegar and, sadly, red food dye, and is used frequently in the cuisine of the Yucatan peninsula. Its mildly sour flavor balances the sweetness of butternut squash.
How do I rub the squash with achiote?
Mix the paste with a small amount of hot water, break it up thoroughly with your hands working in the sink, and rub it on all sides of the squash slabs. Wash your hands afterward, because it stains.
How do you grill the squash and poblanos?

Char the poblanos over direct high heat until mostly black, then steam in a covered bowl for 10 minutes. Reduce the grill heat and cook the squash, flipping halfway, until thoroughly tender, finishing in the microwave if the outside is overcooking.
Why use two tortillas per taco?
Overlapped tortillas make a structurally sound dining device; warm them wrapped in a moistened towel in the microwave for 90 seconds.
How do I make it vegan?
Omit the cheese and the crema.

summary: Warm fava bean (ful) salad with a tart tamarind and Aleppo pepper dressing, two flavors typical of Syrian cuisine: canned fava beans, celery and onion gently warmed, tossed with tamarind, olive oil and parsley; it comes together in about ten minutes.
glance: two 15-ounce cans of fava beans (ful), drained and rinsed
1 tablespoon tamarind concentrate, 1/4 cup olive oil, Aleppo pepper
faq: What kind of fava beans do I need?
The small, round kind about the size of a chickpea, not lima-bean shaped. This recipe uses canned cooked fava beans (ful), drained and rinsed; the author likes the Sahara brand.
What is tamarind?

The pulp from a seed pod that grows on a tropical tree of the same name, best known in Southeast Asian dishes like rasam, sambar and some Pad Thai, but also popular in Syria. You can buy whole pods, a compressed brick, or fully prepared concentrate.
Which tamarind should I buy?

The author uses Tamicon concentrate, which means the salad comes together in ten minutes. Pods or bricks may taste a little better but require hydrating the pulp with boiling water and sieving out strings and seeds.
How tart should the dressing be?
Rather tart. Taste and adjust the salt and Aleppo pepper, and let the salad sit five minutes before a final taste.
What can I use instead of Aleppo pepper?
1/4 teaspoon of cayenne for 1/2 teaspoon of Aleppo.
What do I serve it with?
The author served it with mujadara, roasted cauliflower, tahineh sauce and pita bread.

summary: Cranberry (borlotti) bean "foul mudammas": beans boiled tender, simmered five minutes, then partly crushed in a garlicky lemon and olive oil broth and garnished with cherry tomatoes, green onions and radishes; serves about 4 as a main course.
glance: about 4 as a main course, or more as part of a meze
1.5 cups dry cranberry (borlotti) beans, or 3 cups canned
crush some beans so about half remain semi-whole in a thick broth
faq: What is foul mudammas?

A dish that originated in Egypt and is eaten all over the Middle East and East Africa, spelled many ways (ful medames, fool mudammas). It is most often served for breakfast with flatbread, and there are many variations.
Can I make it with cranberry beans?

The flavor and texture of boiled cranberry (borlotti) beans reminded the author of dried fava beans, so it worked to his taste, though they're not an authentic choice since foul means favas. You can switch back to fava beans.
Can I use canned beans?
Yes, use 3 cups of canned beans of your choice and skip the boiling step.
How do I get the right texture?

Simmer the beans with the garlic, lemon juice, olive oil and salt, then turn off the heat and carefully crush some of the beans with the bottom of a glass so you get a thick broth with about half the beans still semi-whole.
How do I make the garlic paste?
Crush 6 cloves to a paste in a mortar and pestle with a bit of kosher salt, or use a garlic press or a knife.
What are the traditional variations?
Mixes of fava beans and garbanzos, thick as refried beans or thin as soup, insanely garlicky or mild, topped with a hardboiled egg or not.
